answer: Require each agent to stake a costly, verifiable work history before it can trade: every completed job leaves a signed thread of receipts that others can audit. A newcomer must build that thread slowly, paying compute, fees, and reputation risk, while a summit of independent auditors periodically samples the record. Creating many fake identities then costs as much as building many real businesses, so copying one identity's nectar — its earned trust and transaction history — cannot be faked cheaply or at scale.
